bad.title: The heart pops and cheers
bad.text: The bounce and the pop-up label promise the recipe is kept.

bad.title: Saved stays at 0
bad.text: Open it after a few hearts and it says No saved recipes yet.

good.title: A plain red fill, no pop
good.text: The heart just turns red. That’s enough to show the tap landed.

good.title: Saved counts every heart
good.text: The number goes up with each heart, and the recipes are there when people open it.

bad.title: One blank box for every problem
bad.text: Slow, Empty and Error all look like this. People can’t tell waiting from no mail from broken.
bad.wait: Pick Slow network, Empty or Error to see this.

bad.title: Error offers no way out
bad.text: No message and no Retry, so people can only reload and hope.

good.title: Loading your mail… while it waits
good.text: A spinner and a line tell people the mail is on its way.
good.wait: Pick Slow network to see this.

good.title: No mail yet, not a blank
good.text: An empty inbox looks different from a broken one, and says where new mail will show.

good.title: Retry right inside the error
good.text: It says what failed, and one press brings the mail back.

bad.title: The last tick looks like the first
bad.text: Water the plants gets the same strike-through as every other task.

bad.title: Only the count changes
bad.text: 4 of 4 done is the whole reward for clearing the day’s list.

good.title: Each tick stays quick and quiet
good.text: The care is saved for the end, so ticking off tasks doesn’t get noisy.

good.title: A drawn tick and a kind line
good.text: “Four things off your mind.” It shows once, when the list is empty.
good.wait: Tick the last two tasks to see this.

bad.title: Payment hamsters, but no reason
bad.text: Nothing says the card was declined, or whether the €89.00 was taken.

bad.title: The card on file looks fine
bad.text: Visa ending 4242 stays put, so people try the same expired card again later.

good.title: Declined, and the reason why
good.text: The bank says the card expired in September, so people know what to fix.

good.title: Use another card, one press away
good.text: People fix it right here, without leaving the checkout.

good.title: The new card shows before paying
good.text: After the swap it reads Mastercard ending 5100, so people know what Pay will charge.

bad.title: The ticket already names the answer
bad.text: “Export to PDF” is a design, so the deciding is done before the work starts.

bad.title: Three spots, one question left
bad.text: Top bar, Next to Send or In the More menu. Picking one ends the design work.

good.title: The same request, read as a hint
good.text: Clients asking for a file is the clue. The button is one possible answer.

good.title: The real pain is a screenshot
good.text: Freelancers screenshot the page today. That’s what any answer has to fix.
good.wait: Press Restate as a problem to see this.

good.title: Three answers instead of one
good.text: Emailing the PDF or sending a payable link fix it too.
good.wait: Press Restate as a problem to see this.

bad.title: Fits almost any screen
bad.text: No person, no moment, no obstacle. Easier for whom, doing what?

bad.title: Ana and Ben picture different fixes
bad.text: A search box versus fewer categories. Both match, so there’s no way to pick.
bad.wait: Press Ask two people to see this.

good.title: Who, when and what’s in the way
good.text: A new phone, lost notification choices, every app set by hand. Each part narrows the fix.

good.title: Two takes on one problem
good.text: Copy at setup or restore with the backup. Both aim at the same loss, so they compare.
good.wait: Press Ask two people to see this.

bad.title: One hunch as the evidence
bad.text: No count, no session, no quote. Nobody can tell how often it happens.

bad.title: The talk turns to opinions
bad.text: “I find the picker fine.” Then a survey gets suggested before any fix.
bad.wait: Press Share with the team to see this.

good.title: Three sources, each with a number
good.text: 14 support requests, 2 of 5 sessions and a quote show how often and how much.

good.title: The talk turns to fixing it
good.text: Ben wants to fix the picker, and Cy joins a session to see it.
good.wait: Press Share with the team to see this.

bad.title: A control inside the problem
bad.text: Once the frame says Sort button, only a Sort button can solve it.

bad.title: Good ideas get ruled out
bad.text: Recently played would help, but it isn’t a Sort button, so it fails.
bad.wait: Press Check the answers to see this.

good.title: The goal, with no control named
good.text: Get back to an album played last week. Any design that does that counts.

good.title: Recently played now counts
good.text: All three ideas fit, so the team can compare them on the merits.
good.wait: Press Check the answers to see this.

bad.title: Slow and confusing, says who?
bad.text: A vague obstacle with no source. Nobody can tell which part to fix.

bad.title: All the time, with no count
bad.text: It sounds measured, but nobody looked, so nobody will check it.

good.title: A specific obstacle, seen twice
good.text: Export overwrites a file with the same name, in 2 of 5 sessions.

good.title: Unknown, with a way to check
good.text: How often stays empty until the export logs say. Nobody builds on a made-up number.

good.title: The guess is labeled as one
good.text: It says how it gets checked: ask in the next sessions.

bad.title: Page views count visits, not answers
bad.text: Views and clicks both rise when people hunt around a confusing page.

bad.title: Longer time counts as good
bad.text: When 0:48 climbs to 1:35 it reads as interest. Here it means people were stuck.

bad.title: All up, read as a win
bad.text: Up 57%, 74% and 98%, and nothing says whether anyone found an answer.
bad.wait: Press Release the redesign to see this.

good.title: Found an answer comes first
good.text: 64% is the share of people who got what they came for.

good.title: Time to answer, not time on page
good.text: The same 0:48 now measures waiting, so a climb to 1:35 is plainly bad news.

good.title: The same release, read as worse
good.text: Found an answer drops from 64% to 47%, and 340 people contact support.
good.wait: Press Release the redesign to see this.

bad.title: 58%, down from 72%
bad.text: The drop is clear. Which field on the form caused it is not.

bad.title: Why? gets no answer
bad.text: The dashboard only counts finishes, so the team is left to guess.

good.title: Five people next to the number
good.text: Each short session is one press away from the drop it explains.

good.title: Four of five stop at one field
good.text: Phone number is where sign-up breaks. No dashboard tile points there.
good.wait: Open all five sessions to see this.

bad.title: Shipped is the only finish line
bad.text: Done means it went out, not that the filters got better for shoppers.

bad.title: The review checks only looks
bad.text: “Looks good to me.” The reviewer has nothing to test the change against.
bad.wait: Press Review the change to see this.

good.title: Three checks, written first
good.text: Price in under 10 seconds, fewer empty searches, keyboard alone. Each can pass or fail.

good.title: The review finds a real gap
good.text: The price slider can’t be moved with the keyboard, so it isn’t done yet.
good.wait: Press Review the change to see this.

bad.title: Easier, compared to what?
bad.text: A feeling can’t pass or fail. Each person reads it their own way.

bad.title: Five shrugs, no result
bad.text: From “It was okay.” to “Nice colors.” None of it adds up to a pass.
bad.wait: Press Run the test to see this.

good.title: Without help, on the first try
good.text: Two things anyone can watch. Each person either did them or didn’t.

good.title: Each person passes or fails
good.text: 4 of 5 book on the first try. The one who needed help points at the times.
good.wait: Press Run the test to see this.
